product_intent.summary: ThePlanner is a CLI-first planning tool that turns a refined intake brief into a canonical Planning Graph and deterministic repository-native planning artifacts.
target_users: Primary users who want to plan engineering work before implementation
Human engineers reviewing scoped Work Items
Coding agents consuming deterministic execution context
goals: Keep the Planning Graph as the source of truth for requirements, decisions, dependencies, and readiness
Render reviewable Markdown projections for PRDs, RFCs, architecture notes, Work Items, and dependency views
Support safe export, validation, reconciliation, and agent handoff workflows
mvp_scope: Create and validate a typed Planning Graph
Render deterministic projections into repository paths
Prepare and run local coding-agent handoffs with bounded validation
non_goals: Live LLM planning or provider calls during deterministic graph operations
Treating Markdown projections as canonical planning state
Full external tracker synchronization beyond dry-run previews
constraints: Core domain logic must not import CLI, filesystem, process, schema, tracker, or other adapter code
CLI commands must be deterministic and pipeline-friendly
Projection paths must remain stable and workspace-confined
success_criteria: A user can generate, validate, export, and review planning artifacts from a graph without manual rewriting
Work Items include dependencies, validation methods, readiness labels, and traceable requirement links
Dry-run and apply commands report deterministic JSON results

requirements.title: Create a canonical Planning Graph
requirements.statement: The planner must transform an Intake Brief into a typed Planning Graph that is the source of truth for generated artifacts.

requirements.title: Export repository planning artifacts
requirements.statement: The planner must export PRD, RFC, architecture, Work Item, dependency, graph, schema, and validation artifacts into predictable repository paths.

requirements.title: Derive AFK and HITL readiness
requirements.statement: The planner must derive readiness labels from graph inputs and explain why Work Items are AFK-ready, agent-eligible, human-only, HITL-gated, or blocked.

requirements.title: Support graph reconciliation
requirements.statement: The planner must detect edits to exported artifacts and propose safe graph patches or artifact regeneration.

requirements.title: Keep the core independent
requirements.statement: The core planner must not depend on CLI, filesystem, Git, LLM provider, Repo Scan, or schema adapters.

requirements.title: Expose an agent-invocable CLI
requirements.statement: The CLI must support pipeline-friendly commands with JSON output, deterministic paths, non-zero validation exits, and no prompts unless interactive mode is requested.

decisions.title: Planning Graph is canonical
decisions.selected_option: Use planning/graph.json as source of truth and render documents as projections.
decisions.rationale: Prevents drift between PRDs, boards, dependencies, and readiness labels.

decisions.title: Markdown-first repository export
decisions.selected_option: Export local Markdown and structured files before external tracker sync.
decisions.rationale: Keeps V1 local, diffable, credential-free, Git-trackable, and agent-friendly.

decisions.title: Use Hexagonal Architecture
decisions.selected_option: Keep core planner independent from CLI, filesystem, Git, LLM, Repo Scan, schema, and future integration adapters.
decisions.rationale: Improves testability and future reuse across CLI, web, editor, and tracker integrations.

decisions.title: Use TypeScript and Node.js
decisions.selected_option: Implement V1 with TypeScript on Node.js.
decisions.rationale: Fits typed graph modeling, CLI tooling, JSON Schema validation, Markdown generation, and future web/editor reuse.

assumptions.title: Initial implementation will start from an empty repository
assumptions.statement: The repo currently has documentation artifacts but no TypeScript source tree or package manifest.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Generated Work Items may miss existing implementation constraints.

risks.title: Schema minutiae could delay the planning loop
risks.mitigation: Keep the schema draft structural and validate deeper semantics through planned Work Items.

provenance.source_reference: Do not continue into low-level schema minutiae

risks.title: Core may accidentally depend on adapters
risks.mitigation: Add tests or lint rules that fail when src/core imports adapter infrastructure.

open_questions.title: Final public product and CLI name
open_questions.question: Should the public command remain planner or use a distinctive name such as engplanner or specforge?

hitl_gates.title: Approve generated planning artifacts before implementation
hitl_gates.required_action: Primary User reviews and accepts or edits the initial PRD, RFC, architecture, Work Items, dependency view, graph, and schema drafts.
hitl_gates.resolution: Primary User approved generated planning artifacts for implementation.

components.title: Core Domain
components.responsibility: Planning Graph model, validation rules, readiness derivation, projection models, reconciliation rules, and approval rules.

components.title: Application Use Cases
components.responsibility: Orchestrate core logic through ports for planning, validation, export, reconciliation, and status.

components.title: CLI Adapter
components.responsibility: Expose agent-invocable planner commands and pipeline-friendly output.

components.title: Filesystem Export Adapter
components.responsibility: Write deterministic Markdown and structured planning artifacts.

components.title: Schema Adapter
components.responsibility: Validate graph JSON shape with JSON Schema and ajv.

components.title: LLM Adapter
components.responsibility: Propose graph operations without directly mutating canonical state.

components.title: Repo Scan Adapter
components.responsibility: Read repository context explicitly and safely for planning input.

work_items.title: Scaffold TypeScript project and package scripts
acceptance_criteria: package.json defines accepted scripts
tsconfig and source directories exist
planner binary is declared for local development

validation_methods.expected_result: TypeScript compiles without errors after scaffold code exists

work_items.title: Implement core graph types and stable IDs
acceptance_criteria: Core defines V1 node and edge types
Stable typed IDs are modeled
Archived node metadata is represented

work_items.title: Implement graph validation and readiness derivation
acceptance_criteria: Validation reports errors and warnings
AFK-ready cannot be forced when validation fails
Every blocking condition has a regression test

work_items.title: Implement projection rendering
acceptance_criteria: PRD, RFC, architecture, Work Item, and Dependency View projections render from graph input
Work Item files include YAML frontmatter and required sections

work_items.title: Implement CLI command surface
acceptance_criteria: planner plan, validate, export, reconcile, and status commands exist
Commands support --json and deterministic paths
Validation failures use non-zero exit codes

work_items.title: Implement graph reconciliation workflow
acceptance_criteria: Edited projections produce proposed graph patches or conflicts
Mutating reconciliation requires --apply
Manual useful intent is preserved

work_items.title: Implement planning change log
acceptance_criteria: planning/change-log.ndjson records graph changes and approvals
Events include graph version before and after
Events include affected node IDs and rationale

work_items.title: Add dependency-boundary tests
acceptance_criteria: Tests fail if src/core imports adapters, CLI, filesystem, Git, LLM, Repo Scan, or schema adapter code
Boundary tests run in npm test or npm run lint

validation_methods.expected_result: Build, tests, and lint pass with boundary checks enabled

edges.rationale: Scaffold creates the CLI package foundation.
Core graph types implement canonical graph structure.
CLI command surface exposes the accepted agent-invocable planner commands.
Planning change log records changes to the canonical Planning Graph.
Planning change log supports audited reconciliation changes.
CLI validation command needs validation use case.
Change log records graph-changing command flows.
Boundary tests reduce architecture decay risk.
